key_insight: A two-stage deep learning pipeline jointly cancels narrowband interference and produces calibrated soft decisions for OFDM, fixing the mismatch that causes classical demappers to fail after interference mitigation.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces latency and complexity versus compressed-sensing baselines while improving decoding reliability, making it practical for robust OFDM receivers in interference-heavy wireless links.
method: NBI-CNet uses a physics-informed convolutional model to estimate and subtract multi-tone interference in one forward pass.
LLR-CNet converts non-Gaussian post-cancellation residuals into reliable log-likelihood ratios for downstream decoding.
The design is scale-invariant, so it can generalize across FFT sizes without retraining.
evidence_signal: Simulations show the joint framework removes error floors and, at severe interference (SIR = -10 dB), stays within 0.2–0.5 dB of the optimal iterative baseline at BLER = 10^-4, while under mild interference (SIR = 10 dB, Q = 12) it exceeds 3 dB coding gain.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of learned interference and LLR mapping, so deployment should validate robustness to unseen interference statistics and channel conditions.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Joint Narrowband Interference Cancellation and Soft Demodulation in OFDM Systems
